PullRequest.Title: Adding shrink empty lines feature
PullRequest.Body: Fixes #66468 ## Description Adds built-in support for shrinking whitespace-only lines in the editor so more vertical space is available for code. The new `editor.shrinkEmptyLines` setting an arbitrary number value between 0 and 1 where 0 is non-inclusive and 1 is the default. This value is the line height multiplier to use on empty lines. The effective setting resolves to `off` unless `editor.allowVariableLineHeights` is enabled. ## Investigating Visual Studio The main issue references the empty lines shrinking is a feature that already exists in Visual Studio. It can be used using the `Shrink Empty Lines` extension that shrinks the empty lines by 25% vertically making them take up less space. You can see in the image below how this works. The line number is not smaller and because we only shrink by 25% there is no issue with the line numbers overlapping. ## Line Numbers Overlap To fix the line numbers overlap, I will shrink the size of the line number by the same amount as the multiplier so that the line number fits into the space it is inside. Therefore if empty lines are at 0.8 of their default line height, then the line number font size will also be at 0.8. Note this will only take effect when the line height is smaller than the default line height not when it is bigger. ## Manual verification Launch Code OSS and open a text file containing code, empty lines, and lines containing only spaces or tabs. - [x] Confirm the default `editor.shrinkEmptyLines: 1` leaves every line at the regular height. - [x] Set `editor.shrinkEmptyLines` to `0.5`, `0.25`, and another value such as `0.7`; confirm whitespace-only lines use the corresponding proportion of the regular line height and their line numbers scale by the same proportion without overlapping. - [x] Set `editor.shrinkEmptyLines` to `1` and back to `0`; confirm both values leave every line at the regular height. Enter values below `0` and above `1` in settings JSON and confirm the effective value is constrained to the supported `0`–`1` range. - [x] Confirm non-empty lines, including punctuation-only lines and comment lines, retain the regular height and regular line-number font size. - [x] Type text into a compressed line and confirm it immediately returns to the regular height; delete the content again and confirm it immediately becomes compressed. - [x] Make multiline and multi-cursor edits that insert, delete, or replace several lines, then use undo and redo; confirm only whitespace-only lines are compressed after every operation. - [x] Change `editor.lineHeight`, `editor.fontSize`, and the window zoom level while shrinking is enabled; confirm compressed lines and their line numbers continue to scale proportionally. - [x] Disable `editor.allowVariableLineHeights` and confirm all lines return to the regular height; re-enable it and confirm shrinking returns. - [x] Fold a region containing whitespace-only lines and confirm the visible, non-empty fold header keeps the regular height; unfold it and confirm the whitespace-only lines are compressed again. - [x] Navigate across consecutive compressed lines with the keyboard and confirm cursor movement, selection, scrolling, and reveal behavior remain correct.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call path, full-model range, nested N-by-H membership test, and wholesale deltaDecorations call are explicit in the changed code and existing folding/view-model implementation. The exact pause duration depends on file size and enabled setting, which is reflected in medium severity, but the scaling mechanism and UI critical-path reachability are direct.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread CPU work, model-decoration mutations, and temporary decoration objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N model lines and H merged hidden ranges, each fold/unfold synchronously scans all N lines and the per-line hiddenAreas.some check performs up to H tests, making the added work O(N*H), plus O(B) decoration replacement for B whitespace-only lines. Ordinary edits similarly pay O(C*H) for C changed lines.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased input/folding latency and dropped frames while folding or editing large structured files with many collapsed regions
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, hidden-area changes did not trigger a second full-document content scan or wholesale replacement of empty-line line-height decorations; folding only performed the editor's existing hidden-range update.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added onDidChangeHiddenAreas listener synchronously calls _updateAllDecorations. That method passes the entire model to _getDecorations, which trims every line, runs hiddenAreas.some for every line, and replaces all tracked decorations even when one fold changed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 44 registers `this.editor.onDidChangeHiddenAreas(() => this._updateAllDecorations())`, newly placing the controller's whole-model scan and decoration replacement on every fold/unfold event.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding every empty-line decoration on each fold change
Findings.Impact: With shrinkEmptyLines enabled, toggling a fold in a large file (for example, tens of thousands of lines with hundreds or thousands of collapsed regions) can block the UI while the controller rechecks the entire file and churns every blank-line decoration. Typing also scans the complete hidden-range list for each changed line.
Findings.Evidence: The new listener at line 44 directly invokes _updateAllDecorations on every HiddenAreasChanged event. _updateAllDecorations constructs range 1..model.getLineCount(), and _getDecorations nests its line loop with hiddenAreas.some before calling trim/getLineContent. Hidden ranges are normalized into sorted, non-overlapping ranges by viewModelLines.normalizeLineRanges, so H can remain large and the current search does not exploit that ordering. FoldingController.onHiddenRangesChanges synchronously calls editor.setHiddenAreas, which emits HiddenAreasChanged, placing this work on the fold interaction path. Decoration replacement also emits per-line line-height changes into the view layout.
Findings.Recommendation: Track the previous normalized hidden ranges and update only lines whose visibility changed. For full rebuilds, traverse the sorted hidden ranges with a monotonic index (and use binary search for isolated edited lines) rather than calling some for every line; preserve existing decorations outside affected ranges.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or attach a text model with shrinkEmptyLines enabled, and change shrink/line-height configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The eager editor contribution constructor and relevant synchronous configuration listener call _updateAllDecorations before the editor settles, scanning model lines and applying line-height decorations. This work is on the editor/model setup or configuration interaction critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total model lines N, whitespace-only lines B, and currently merged hidden ranges H; the implementation scans N lines, performs up to N*H hidden-range predicates, and creates/replaces B decorations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous on the editor main thread; no scheduler, limiter, coalescing, or parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No scan or classification cache is used. Every full update rereads and trims line content and rebuilds the decoration list; warm runs have the same algorithmic work as cold runs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor/configuration call sites and full-model loops are explicit; no external boundary assumptions are needed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The setting is opt-in and exact latency depends on model size and collapsed-range count, but large source/generated files make the multiplicity realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: The initial scan is required to realize the enabled feature, but its nested hidden-range membership check contributes to the reported scaling mechanism. Configuration changes are less frequent than folding and do not warrant a separate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type, paste, multi-cursor edit, undo, or redo while shrinking is enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: onDidChangeModelContent synchronously maps changed ranges, queries old decorations, checks each affected line against hidden ranges, and mutates decorations before the content event path completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Changed lines C after event mapping, merged hidden ranges H, and model decorations intersecting those changed ranges; hidden membership scales as C*H without deduplication/coalescing of overlapping changed ranges.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous serial work on each model-content event; no debounce or coalescing across rapid input events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Decoration IDs are retained, but line emptiness and hidden membership are recomputed for every event. There is no negative/positive classification cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event listener and loops are direct. Common single-line edits usually keep the cost modest, while files with many hidden ranges amplify it.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical typing changes one line, so impact depends primarily on how many regions are concurrently hidden; bulk edits increase C.
Scenarios.Verdict: The per-edit H scan is part of the same reported hidden-range lookup issue; no separate finding was submitted to avoid duplicate comments.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fold or unfold regions while shrinking is enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Folding synchronously calls editor.setHiddenAreas, emits onDidChangeHiddenAreas, and the new listener immediately runs _updateAllDecorations before the interaction can render.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: N total lines, H normalized disjoint hidden ranges, and B whitespace-only lines. A single fold toggle adds an O(N*H) membership scan and O(B) decoration replacement.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous main-thread execution with no deferment, incremental visibility diff, cancellation, batching, or coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Previous empty-line classification and decorations are discarded/reprocessed wholesale. Warm cache state does not reduce work, and each fold event repeats it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the folding-to-hidden-event path, whole-model range, nested hidden-area search, and decoration mutation are all established in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The largest pauses require both the feature and large/fold-heavy files; precise duration is environment-dependent, supporting medium severity rather than uncertainty in the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable introduced regression; submitted a finding anchored to the added hidden-area listener.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll or render viewport line numbers with variable line heights
Scenarios.CriticalPath: LineNumbersOverlay.prepareRender now calls getLineHeightForLineNumber and conditionally appends a font-size style for each visible line before overlay HTML is emitted.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible viewport line count V and number of custom-height lines B; each lookup is a binary search over custom lines, so added work is O(V log B), bounded by the viewport.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous render-loop work; no async boundaries or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The line-height manager maintains ordered custom-line data and commits pending changes once; line-number HTML is regenerated under the existing overlay render lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added lookup, low that it creates material user-visible regression because cardinality is viewport-bounded and the operation is in-memory.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact render frequency and viewport size vary, but V is small and bounded, and similar line-height lookups already occur in variable-height rendering paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this is necessary viewport-bounded rendering work and lacks evidence of a concrete material regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch models or dispose an editor containing shrink decorations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CodeEditorWidget disposes model contributions during detach and removes all decorations owned by the editor; controller disposal also requests removal of tracked IDs.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number B of shrink decorations owned by that editor/model.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Decoration ownership is scoped by editor ID; detached models remove all owner decorations, so tracked state is not retained across model lifetime unintentionally.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High based on changeDecorations owner IDs and _postDetachModelCleanup calling removeAllDecorationsWithOwnerId.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cleanup time scales with enabled-feature decoration count, but it is bounded by model-owned state and does not leak across switches.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup-lifecycle finding: model switching and disposal remove the introduced decorations rather than retaining them.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all seven changed files and traced editor creation/model attachment, configuration, content edits, folding, disposal/model switching, and viewport rendering. One introduced synchronous scaling regression was reported: fold changes rebuild all empty-line decorations while performing a per-line linear hidden-range search. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries are reached by these paths, and no concrete performance-regression fix requiring blame was present.
